annotation.title_en: The Cake Money and the Traffic Cop
annotation.summary_en: A desperate traffic police officer, pressured by his wife to bring home a birthday cake despite no traffic, finally stops a driver and forces him to pay for an impromptu dance.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch opens on a narrow, rural roadside where a traffic police officer (Sergeant Khachatryan) is stationed. He receives a phone call from his wife, who reminds him that tomorrow is their child's birthday. When she insists he must not return home without a birthday cake, he complains that business has been non-existent all day on this quiet road. Just as he hangs up, a driver approaches in a new car. The officer excitedly remarks that a 'cake' is coming to him on its own wheels. He stops the driver and conducts a thorough inspection, checking for a driver's license, technical passport, inspection sticker, and a first-aid kit. To the officer's frustration, the driver is perfectly law-abiding and has every required item. Desperate for money, the officer asks if the car has a radio. When the driver confirms, the officer tells him to turn it on. In an absurd turn, the officer begins dancing violently in front of (and eventually on) the car, brandishing a weapon, and demands payment from the bewildered driver for the 'performance.'
catchphrases: Ի՞նչ ես էշցած նայում արա, չես տենում քո համար եմ պարում, փող տուր փող։
